title: Chapter 3 Quiz 13
description: Splitting a program into smaller parts and calling them.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **subprogram**?
options: A kind of variable with a name
A named part run when called
A type of file stored on disk
A program that runs on its own
questions.explanation: A subprogram has a name, variables, instructions, a beginning and an end. Watch out: unlike a program, it cannot execute independently.

questions.question: Which instruction asks for the execution of a subprogram?
questions.explanation: The main program (or another subprogram) uses CALL.

questions.question: Which are advantages of subprograms?
questions.explanation: The course lists reusability, modularity and clarity. Watch out: a program with subprograms is not necessarily shorter to type.

questions.question: Match each subprogram word to its description.
right: Does actions with no returned value
Sends the result back to the caller
Requests the execution of a subprogram
questions.explanation: These are the key words of subprograms.

questions.question: Which is a **function**?
options: Clear_Screen, which only wipes the screen
DisplayArea(radius), which only displays the area
Display('Hello'), which only shows a text
questions.explanation: A function provides a result. The others only perform an action. Watch out: DisplayArea calculates, but it displays the result instead of returning it.

questions.question: Which call makes **no sense**, since the subprogram returns no value?
questions.explanation: DisplayArea is a procedure, so there is nothing to store in a. Watch out: Call GetCircumference(r) is allowed, but its result would be lost.

questions.question: In GetCircumference with PI = 3.14, what is returned for radius = 5? (2 × PI × radius)
In DisplayArea with PI = 3.14, what area is displayed for radius = 5? (PI × radius × radius)
questions.explanation: 3.14 × 25 = 78.5. Watch out: it is radius × radius, not radius × 2.

questions.question: Complete the function that returns the sum of two numbers.
questions.code:
Function Sum(a, b) {{1}} Integer
Begin
    {{2}} a + b
End Function
questions.explanation: A function declares the type it returns with Returns and sends the value back with Return.

questions.question: This function should return the circumference of a circle (2 × PI × radius). One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function GetCircumference(radius) Returns Real
Begin
    Constant PI ← 3.14
    Return 2 * PI + radius
End Function
questions.explanation: The circumference is 2 × PI × radius. Watch out: with + the function would return 8.14 for radius 5 instead of 31.4.

questions.question: A procedure can be called only once in a program.
questions.explanation: A subprogram can be called as many times as needed. That is the point of reusing it. Watch out: the number of calls is not limited.
